# Political Ideology Atlas

> A free political ideology test at https://ideologyatlas.fyi/. It finds the dividing lines between
> ideologies from sourced audits of how each ideology answers a few hundred statements, then matches
> the user's answers against them. Source code, data and audits: https://github.com/brioja/political-ideology-atlas

The site is a single page whose results are worked out by its script in the browser. Fetching a
result link without running the script shows only the empty shell, not the result.

Every ideology and person also has a plain page that reads fine without the script:
`https://ideologyatlas.fyi/ideologies/<id>/` and `https://ideologyatlas.fyi/people/<id>/` (summary,
key positions, closest ideologies and people). All of them are listed in https://ideologyatlas.fyi/sitemap.xml.

## Result links

A result link looks like `https://ideologyatlas.fyi/?r=3.<answers>`. It carries the person's answers
and nothing else. After `3.`, each character is one statement, in the order listed in
https://raw.githubusercontent.com/brioja/political-ideology-atlas/main/audits/share-slots.json
(the `slots` array of statement ids): `-` = not answered, `0` = strongly disagree, `1` = disagree,
`2` = neither, `3` = agree, `4` = strongly agree. Trailing unanswered statements are dropped.
Statement texts are in https://raw.githubusercontent.com/brioja/political-ideology-atlas/main/statements.json
(match by `id`).

The ideology match itself depends on the model built from every audit, so it can't be read off the
link alone. If someone shares only a link, decode their answers as above, and ask them to open the
link in a browser and paste what the results page shows (closest ideologies, people and dividing lines).
